author: maddie-j
title: Cannot use Win + Space when swapping from PowerToys Run to Command Palette

judgment.rationale: The live thread now includes a same-user report that Win+Space fails while PowerToys runs as administrator and works after switching to user mode. Earlier reports show other outcomes, including success only with the low-level hook, failure despite that setting, Start-menu dependence, and a double-Space workaround. This is a concrete elevation-sensitive reproduction, but the failing registration or hook mechanism is still unconfirmed.
evidence: The original reporter said Win+Space worked in PowerToys Run but not Command Palette on the same system.
Some reports say enabling the low-level keyboard hook fixed the issue; other reports say the option did not help.
One user reports the shortcut works only when Start is already open; another needs two Space presses.
The newest report says Win+Space and Win+W fail in admin mode and work after switching PowerToys to user mode.
Current MainWindow.SetupHotkey first unregisters old hotkeys, then routes configured hotkeys through the low-level keyboard listener or RegisterHotKey according to settings.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the same Win+Space binding under user and administrator modes on the current build, then trace which registration and callback path differs before selecting a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The latest admin-versus-user comparison adds an elevation-dependent branch worth fixing, but earlier reports conflict about hook settings and focus, so the exact failing mechanism must be established first.

proposed_fixes.title: Make CmdPal Win+Space activation reliable when PowerToys runs elevated
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: elevated execution changes whether the configured Win+Space registration or low-level hook receives and consumes the chord. The current discussion demonstrates an admin/user difference for one reporter, but does not establish whether hook installation, callback delivery, or summon handling is responsible.
plan: Add focused diagnostics for the selected registration mode, hook startup result, and matched-command callback without recording user keystrokes or text.
Reproduce the same configured chord in user and administrator modes and identify whether registration, low-level-hook delivery, or command summoning diverges.
Fix the confirmed elevated-mode branch so one Win+Space chord opens Command Palette and does not also trigger the Windows input switcher, while preserving unrelated Windows-key shortcuts.
Add regression coverage for admin and user mode with the low-level hook both enabled and disabled.
verification: With the same machine and settings, compare Win+Space in PowerToys user mode and administrator mode; record whether CmdPal opens, Windows switches language, or neither occurs.
Repeat from the desktop and with Start open, with the low-level hook both enabled and disabled.
Confirm Win+Alt+Space and unrelated Windows-key shortcuts remain functional.

confidence.rationale: The newly reported privilege-mode difference is useful but comes from one reporter; prior reports conflict and the current source path does not identify which layer fails.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette inconsistently loses the configured Win+Space chord; the newest report says it works in user mode but fails when PowerToys runs as administrator.
known_information: The original report used Win+Space successfully in PowerToys Run but not in Command Palette.
Reports differ on whether the low-level keyboard hook, Start-menu focus, or a second Space press changes the outcome.
The October 2026 report says Win+Space and Win+W fail in admin mode and work after switching to user mode.
Current CmdPal hotkey setup clears existing registrations and selects either its low-level keyboard listener or RegisterHotKey path based on settings.
inferences: The newest result suggests an elevation-sensitive registration or callback issue, but it does not prove which Windows or CmdPal component owns the failed chord.
The inconsistent focus and repeated-key outcomes may be separate manifestations or separate configurations.
issue_context.analysis: The newly supplied admin-versus-user comparison changes the reproduction matrix but is not enough to justify a specific hook patch. Compare the same build and settings across privilege modes, record the selected registration path, and then target the branch that fails.
initial_investigation: Re-read all eight live comments, including the October admin-mode update.
Inspected current MainWindow.SetupHotkey, which unregisters prior hotkeys and selects between low-level listener and RegisterHotKey based on the configured option.
Inspected the low-level listener and native hook startup/error path; no evidence currently isolates the failure to hook registration versus callback delivery.
Checked prior hotkey changes referenced by the previous triage; they did not resolve the conflicting current reports.

design.title: Make CmdPal Win+Space activation reliable when elevated

actions.label: Compare Win+Space in admin and user modes
actions.note: The latest report gives a direct same-user privilege-mode comparison; verify the registration path before implementing a fix.

reproduce.title: Compare CmdPal Win+Space behavior across privilege modes
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys or current main
prerequisites: Command Palette enabled and PowerToys Run disabled.
Win+Space configured as the Command Palette activation shortcut.
At least two Windows keyboard layouts so the Windows input switcher has an observable action.
steps: In user mode, test Win+Space once from the desktop and record whether Command Palette opens or Windows switches language.
Run the same build as administrator without changing settings and repeat; include Win+W as the secondary reported shortcut.
Repeat both modes with the low-level keyboard hook enabled and disabled.
Repeat with Start closed and open, and compare the selected mode and any hook-start failure reported by CmdPal.
reproduce.expected_result: With equivalent configuration, the supported registration mode should activate Command Palette exactly once and should not also trigger the Windows input switcher; any unsupported mode should fail with an explicit registration diagnostic.
